# Restaurant Table Reservation System (RTRS)

Multi-tenant restaurant and salon reservation SaaS operated by **Vibespot Technologies Ltd. (Ghana)**
Built with Node + Express + Sequelize + MySQL backend and Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite frontend.
Ghana locale (GHS), Paystack payments, WhatsApp ordering, ShaQ Express delivery, DPA 2012 compliance.
Single-tenant by default; multi-tenant platform code lives under `back-end/src/tenant-platform/` and is gated behind `TENANT_MODE=enabled`.

## Agent Instructions

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): Project conventions, verification commands, recommended skills, and critical constraints (do not commit unless asked, do not reintroduce NOT NULL/PARTITION BY on `tenantId`, sync Obsidian vault after work, refresh this file on architecture shifts).

## Architecture

- **Monorepo layout**: `back-end/` (Express + Sequelize + Redis/BullMQ + Socket.IO) and `front-end/` (Vue 3 + Pinia + Vuestic UI).
- **Multi-tenant mode**: activated by `TENANT_MODE=enabled`. Tenant context resolved by `resolveTenant` middleware; all tenant-platform code under `back-end/src/tenant-platform/`.
- **Three frontend entry points** (Vite dev servers):
  - Super-admin portal: `front-end/vite.config.super-admin.js` → port `8080`
  - Tenant portal: `front-end/vite.config.tenant.js` → port `8081`
  - Customer portal: `front-end/vite.config.customer.js` → port `8082`
  All three load the same `front-end/src/main.ts` Vue app. `App.vue` is now a thin error-boundary wrapper; each portal uses its own layout:
  - Super-admin: `SuperAdminLayout.vue` (`.sa-sidebar`)
  - Tenant: `TenantLayout.vue` (`.tl-sidebar`)
  - Customer/standalone: inline `standalone-sidebar` or `CustomerLandingView.vue`
- **Router**: `front-end/src/router/index.js` — standalone routes (landing, login, register, customer portal) plus conditionally added admin/tenant/salon routes. Super-admin routes are nested under `/super-admin` with `SuperAdminLayout`; tenant routes under `/admin` with `TenantLayout`. Customer portal routes use `standalone: true`.
- **Auth store**: `front-end/src/stores/auth.ts` — login, logout, getMe, settings, tenant mode, capabilities, refresh token, locale. `logout()` resets user, entryPoint, and currentTenant. `fetchTenantMode()` reuses `fetchSettings()`.
- **API interceptor**: `front-end/src/services/API.js` — queues concurrent 401s so only one refresh-token request is in flight at a time; unauthenticated `/auth/locale` requests are no longer fired from `App.vue` to avoid 401 noise.
- **Design system**: `front-end/src/assets/base.css` and `front-end/src/assets/design-system.css` define CSS custom properties for brand palette (warm browns + amber accent), typography (Fraunces + Public Sans), spacing, radius, shadows, and Vuestic overrides. JS mirror tokens in `front-end/src/theme/colors.js`. Tenant branding white-labels via CSS variables (`useTenantBranding.js`).
- **Security hardening**: Tenant-platform controllers use explicit field allowlists to prevent mass assignment (`alertRule`, `autoScalingTrigger`, `caseStudy`, `complianceEvidence`, `incident`, `subProcessor`, `dataRetentionPolicy`, `platformReferral`, `marketplace`, `encryptionKey`). `sync.service.js` validates POS sync URLs against private/loopback IPs to prevent SSRF. `monitoring.controller.js` returns generic error messages to avoid information disclosure. `platformAudit.router.js` `/recent` requires `manage_tenants` permission.

- Public: `/`, `/customer`, `/login`, `/register`, `/menu`, `/checkout`, `/about`, `/legal/:slug`

- Customer portal: `/portal`, `/portal/profile`, `/portal/reservations`, `/portal/orders`, `/portal/appointments` (salon), `/portal/gift-cards` (salon), `/portal/referrals` (salon), `/portal/packages` (salon)
- Salon vertical: `/appointments`, `/stations`, `/station-map`, `/services`, `/packages`, `/gift-cards`, `/referrals`, `/locations`, `/inventory`, `/expenses`, `/pricing`, `/salon/*` (settings, walkins, calendar, shifts, schedule, holidays, reports, recurring, clients, marketing, gallery, unified-schedule, whatsapp-bookings, whatsapp-payments, dashboard, staff)
- Tenant login by slug: `/t/:tenantSlug/login`
- Customer portal by slug: `/t/:tenantSlug/portal`

## External Integrations

- **Paystack**: GHS payments (Mobile Money, cards, bank). Platform-managed keys; rotation endpoint at `/api/v1/admin/paystack/keys/rotate`.
- **WhatsApp Business**: Ordering confirmations and support chat.
- **ShaQ Express**: Delivery partner integration with order-conversion analytics.
- **Socket.IO**: Real-time updates for reservations, orders, and support chat.

## Development Commands

```bash
# Backend
cd back-end && npm test               # Jest suite (forceExit)
npm run migrate:up                    # Apply Sequelize migrations
npm run start:dev                     # Nodemon + migrations
npm run seed:all                      # Seed database

# Frontend
cd front-end && npm run dev           # Default Vite dev server
npm run dev:super-admin               # Super-admin portal on :8080
npm run dev:tenant                    # Tenant portal on :8081
npm run dev:customer                  # Customer portal on :8082
npm run build                         # Production build
npm run lint                          # ESLint + Prettier (auto-fix)
npm run test:unit                     # Vitest (jsdom)
npm run test:a11y                     # Playwright accessibility
npm run test:visual                   # Playwright visual regression
npm run test:e2e                      # Playwright E2E
```

## Verification Gates

- **Backend**: `cd back-end && npm test` — 447 Jest tests; must stay green (catches cross-tenant leaks and RBAC regressions).
- **Frontend**: `cd front-end && npm run lint && npm run build && npm run test:unit` — lint, build, and 22 unit tests must pass.
- **Migrations**: `npm run migrate:up` — replays from earliest unapplied migration; keep `up()` idempotent.
- **Dependency advisories**: Dependabot PRs are merged after review; recent example: postcss 8.5.23 security patch (source-map path-traversal fix).
- **Versioning**: `VERSION` file at repo root tracks current release; git tags mark release boundaries (e.g., `v1.1.0`).
